units.author: dc_7_irena
units.text: Dear Benedikt, I listened this morning with my reading glasses on, which I realise does not help the ears. I heard your keys, and your feet, and then the three others. They are the ones I hear when I come down from 8 at half past six. They are lighter than a man's. They stop when I stop. I have nothing more to add, but I did not want you to feel alone in it. Irena, 7C

units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: I have listened to it. I hear a man coming down concrete stairs with his keys out and the echo of a man coming down concrete stairs with his keys out. I drove buses through the Canal Street underpass for twenty-two years. Everything echoes in concrete. The hum is the lift motor, which isn't working, which is why he is on the stairs. Case closed.

units.author: dc_6_jordie
units.text: respectfully mr pryce the lift motor is in the roof plant room and it's been off for a week, I know because I put my ear to the door for a laugh. so not the lift. echo is fair though, I'm an engineering student and echoes are like 40% of my degree. gonna do a clap test on the stairs tomorrow in daylight

units.author: dc_8_benedikt
units.text: Thank you, Irena. Mr Pryce, maybe it is echo, I don't know. I put the recording on LowBand tonight, they have people who measure sound. Someone already says there is a fridge compressor in it. I say again: there isn't a fridge on that floor. I went and looked tonight with Hassan's torch. Bins. Nothing humming.

units.author: dc_12_ollie
units.text: i listened with my mum and she made me turn it off. my friend Sami on 4 says the steps are the man who counts you, from the story, and he counts the steps you dont take. i dont believe that. my mum says the roof door was open again this morning, she saw it when she took the bins up

units.author: dellow_admin
units.text: Ollie, love, please leave stories from school off the board for now, they upset the little ones. The roof door I will add to the meeting list, thank you, that's a proper safety issue. And to all of you: thank you for the times and dates. I've got eleven entries so far. The Post rang me today; I told them it's a maintenance issue, which is still an issue. Bev, DCRA

units.author: dc_11_soraya
units.text: I haven't listened and I don't think I will, if that's all right. I'm sure it's useful for the meeting. I'll just say we walked down singing again today and nobody waited for us on 7, according to R. He says the man had 'gone to work'. Little M. wants to know what job he does. I said the night shift.

units.author: dc_14_ivy
units.text: Tobin format, for the table: 1. last night; 2. 02:20; 3. up (fetching a sketchbook I'd left in the laundry room, yes, at 2am, don't); 4. 1 to 14; 5. off between 7 and 8; 6. steps above me, going up, past 13 and 14, and then the roof door bar going 'clack'; 7. n. I stood on 14 and nobody came down. (Drew it afterwards. Bad drawing.)

units.author: dc_9_tobin
units.text: Logged. Entries so far, n=9, all between 21:30 and 06:40. 7 of 9 involve the 6 to 8 section with lights off. 2 of 9 report steps continuing after the poster stopped. 1 of 9 (yours) reports steps above 13. The roof door noise is new. I'd recommend we ask Kerrow Estates whether the door has an alarm log.

units.author: dc_8_benedikt
units.text: Tobin format: 1. day 5; 2. 23:10; 3. down; 4. 8 to 6; 5. off between 8 and 7; 6. my steps, then about three more above me after I stopped on 7; 7. n. Recording is on the other thread. Sorry I did not do it in this format before.

units.author: dc_2_hassan
units.text: The urn is booked. Also, for the list though it is not about stairs: the delivery van in the visitor bays belongs to a driver who sleeps in it between shifts. I spoke to him. He is very polite and buys milk. I think he will move if asked nicely. Mr Pryce, please ask nicely. H

units.author: dc_14_ivy
units.text: As promised: the laundry room at 1am. Ink and wash. Machine 2 with its door open like a mouth (affectionate), Jordie's bag of washing on the bench, the strip light buzzing (drawn as little lines, cartoon-style), and a sign that says 'Please remove your lint' which someone has corrected to 'your lintel'. Least frightening room in the building. Confirmed.

units.author: dc_5_lorna
units.text: Oh I love that love, the lintel was me, I'm sorry, I was bored waiting for the dryer at half five, and you've got Jordie's washing exactly, it's been on that bench since Tuesday, somebody tell him, anyway I'm off up to bed now the sun's thinking about it

units.title: Stairwell recording, Dellow Court, Weyhaven (phone, sorry)
units.author: dc_8_benedikt
units.text: Hello. I am not a recordist, I am a delivery driver. Our building's residents' board said to ask you. Day 5, 23:10, phone in my hand, walking down the stairwell from 8 to 6 when the lights go out. I stop on 7. Steps carry on above me, three or so. File attached, it is the copy from my phone chat, so compressed. Is there a way to know what this is? Thank you.

units.author: lowband_mod
units.text: Welcome, Benedikt, and thank you for posting clearly with time and place, which puts you ahead of most first posts. If you can, put up the original file from the phone itself, not the chat copy, which smears everything. In the meantime, people: comments on the recording only, please. This is not a ghost thread.

units.title: Dellow file: first impression (the hum)
units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: First impression only, proper analysis tomorrow on the full file. Underneath the steps there's a low hum that cycles on and off, roughly a minute on and a quarter off. That's very likely a compressor: fridge, chiller, dehumidifier, something with refrigerant. Structure-borne hum carries well up a concrete riser. I'd look for it before looking for anything else.

units.author: dc_8_benedikt
units.text: Thank you. But there isn't a fridge on that floor. Floor 8 at that end is the bin store. I looked tonight again. Bins, a mop, a dead light. Nothing on. The flats on 8 have kitchens on the other side, away from the stairs.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Understood, and I believe you that there's no fridge in the bin store. But 'not on that floor' isn't the same as 'not in the riser'. A compressor on 6, 9 or 10, or in a flat backing onto the stairwell wall, or in the shop below, could put that hum into the concrete. I'm not saying the steps are a fridge. I'm saying the hum is a machine.

units.author: dc_8_benedikt
units.text: Maybe. The hum is not what I care about. I care about the steps after I stop. But you are right that it is a machine sound and I will ask. There isn't a fridge on that floor, though. I want that written down so nobody says I did not check.

units.author: hobby_binaural
units.text: Oh, I know Dellow Court, I've done a binaural walk down Canal Street past it. First listen on earbuds on the bus home: the extra steps have a very different placement to yours, Benedikt, which is interesting. Not saying anything until I've had proper headphones on for this one. Tomorrow, on decent cans.

units.author: nightscream_vlog
units.text: guys this is insane. footsteps that keep going after you stop?? in a tower block?? benedikt can i use this on my channel, ill put some ambience over it and credit you. also which floor, im thinking a live overnight in the stairwell, link in bio

units.author: lowband_mod
units.text: No. Nobody's files go on anybody's channel without the owner's written permission, and never with 'ambience' over them. And nobody is doing a live stream in a residential building where people live, including a 74-year-old who uses those stairs. NightScream, you've been here a day. Please read the housekeeping thread before posting again.

units.author: dc_8_benedikt
units.text: No, thank you. It is for my neighbours, not for a channel. Please do not come to the building.

units.author: hobby_tapeloop
units.text: Young man, I was very taken with your clock correction. In my day it was the tape speed that betrayed you: a machine running slow on cold batteries would make a whole night's timings drift. I mention it only because I have found my box of reservoir tapes, from the dam works, and I believe there is one of machinery knocking at night. I will get the lead from the archivist. Regards, Ned

units.author: brackwater_keeper
units.text: Estate nursery has no frost protection, it's a shed and some saplings. The water company does run the outflow valves at night some weeks, I've seen the van. Nothing on a timer that I know of at twenty to three. Whatever it is, the gate stays locked at dusk. I'll see you at the office, as arranged.

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Thank you, both. Ned, I'd love to hear the dam tape when the lead arrives, it would be a proper control. Keeper, understood on the gate. Tonight's file from the footpath: nothing. Owls, the outflow hiss, a fox at 01:15 and a car on the reservoir road at 02:05. No knocks at 02:40. Kit as before. Make of it what you will.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: ok so a nothing night is still data, right? I'm going out to the pumping house end in the next couple of nights, I'll sync my recorder clock to yours first so nobody can say anything about clocks. (I will check the year this time.)

units.title: Fog week: share your fog recordings
units.author: hobby_hydrophone
units.text: Starting a share thread. Mine: hydrophone off the end of Gilliver pontoon last night, 20:00 to 21:30. Ferry props approaching from about three miles out, clear as a bell underwater while you couldn't see the boat above. A creel boat's winch. A lot of crackle from shrimp, which in November I didn't expect. And a mooring chain somewhere knocking on the turn of the tide. No mysteries. Just water.

units.author: hobby_binaural
units.text: Love this. Mine: a binaural walk along the canal towpath at nine, headphones on for this one. The fog makes the city very close and very small. You hear a bike bell in front of you, then right beside your left ear, then gone. The tower blocks sound like they're breathing, which is mostly extractor fans. Uploading tonight.

units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: Catalogue note: fog recordings are under-represented in the archive, so please tag anything from this week with 'fog' and the visibility if you know it. The 1982 Lisle pier file, LB-0371, is the closest comparison we have for ferry signals. Ned, the line-out lead is in the post.

units.title: A van outside the bakery all night
units.author: lh_baker_coriveth
units.text: Small mystery from the ovens. A white van parked outside the bakery at about 01:30, engine running, no lights. Still there when the first tray of loaves came out at 02:40, still there at four. Nobody got out. Nobody came to the window for the warm rolls, which on a cold night in a harbour town is honestly the strangest part. Smelled like diesel and rye.

units.author: lh_dockguard_coriveth
units.text: I walk past the bakery on the 04:00 roll run. Will note the plates and whether anyone's in it. Gate 7 log tonight: monitor 6 clear, NE yard patrolled 01:00 and 03:00, nil found. IT have the dropped-frame note. Thank you for the poppy seed yesterday.

units.author: lh_security_st
units.text: You've got one too! Mine's in Weyhaven, so not the same van, before anyone starts. Our best theory, thanks to a picker on here, is a driver sleeping in the back with the engine on for the heater. Empty cab, engine running, no lights. Knock on the side if you're braver than me. I wasn't.

units.author: lh_baker_coriveth
units.text: A sleeping driver is a lovely idea and I'd like to believe it. If he's asleep in the back, he's asleep about three metres from fresh bread, which is a tragedy. I've put a roll in a paper bag on the step by the van. If it's gone in the morning, we'll know someone's in there. Back to the dough.

units.title: The front door intercom and Mrs A.
units.author: lh_carer_vellmark
units.text: I'm writing this in the quiet room. The front door intercom at the home buzzed at 03:10. Nobody at the door; the camera showed the step and the frost. Mrs A., who was sitting up in the lounge, patted my hand and said 'that's for me, love'. It's the third night it's buzzed at ten past three. She's said the same thing each time. I'm sorry, I just wanted to tell someone.

units.author: lh_nurse_halvard
units.text: Oh, intercom sisters. Ours keeps calling a discharged patient's name, which turned out at least partly to be the system remembering the wrong bed record. Yours may be a fault too. Old intercoms buzz with damp in the junction box when it gets cold, and three is the coldest hour. And residents often say things like that. It's kind of you to sit with her. Back to it.

units.author: lh_miner_vellmark
units.text: She's my partner, so I'll say it for her: she's right to post and she worries too much about posting. I'll get an electrician mate to look at the box at the weekend. Up top, minus five. Bus driver's still nodding.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: Agree with the nurse and the miner both. A buzz at the same minute each night points to something on a schedule or a temperature threshold. As for Mrs A.: people near the end of a long life often say quite certain things at night, and it helps them more than any explanation does to be sat with. You're doing the right thing.

units.author: lh_kennel_orrin
units.text: Good thoughts, Dmitra. No ultrasonic pest thing that I know of, but there's an old fluorescent tube at the far end that flickers. I've put a note for Pete. Tonight: Biscuit sat at the door again at 02:10. Juno too. Ziggy, who is a Great Dane and afraid of nothing, walked halfway and came back to me and leaned. They're fine in the front runs. I'm not reading anything into it.

units.author: lh_trucker_orrin
units.text: A Great Dane leaning on you is a dog asking for a cuddle, not a ghost story, so you got a cuddle out of it at least. That tube'd be my bet. Old ones whine like a mosquito when they're going, and a dog's ears are better than any of ours. Coffee's on me Thursday.

units.author: lh_callcentre_tamsin
units.text: night six. a man who's convinced the power company can see him through the meter. sir, if we could, we wouldn't watch you. a woman who wanted to know if fog 'gets into the wires' (not over here, there's no fog here, she was watching the news about the north). and a sweet old boy who rang to say his lights were working and he just wanted to say thank you. I logged it as a fault, because I didn't have a code for joy.

units.author: lh_lighttender_tamsin
units.text: Hana, the old boy who rang to say thank you will stay with me all night on the gallery. We have the same coast, and tonight is clear and still, with the beam going out a long way over the water. There ought to be a code for joy. In the meantime, a fault will do.

units.title: Housekeeping: week one
units.author: lh_mod
units.text: Housekeeping, weekly. 1. Lovely threads this week: callers, fares, kennels, bakeries. More of that. 2. Lamp Hours is company on the night shift, not campfire stories; logs of odd things are fine, prophecy isn't. 3. If you're posting at 4am because you can't sleep, drink a glass of water first. 4. Be kind to the new people. 5. I'm on until six. Ines.

units.author: lh_porter_portammet
units.text: Glass of water drunk. Second glass drunk. Now I need the loo, which on B corridor at this hour is a 300-metre trek past the lift that sings. Thanks Ines. Also, A&E tonight: a man from Gilliver who walked into a bollard on Harbour Road because the street lights are out. Mended. Embarrassed.

units.author: lh_taxi_halvard
units.text: water drunk, Ines, though mine came from the cafe kettle so it's technically tea. quiet night on the rank, one fare who wanted to go 'anywhere with a view of the river' at 3am and then sat in silence looking at it for ten minutes and paid double. I didn't ask. anyway

units.author: lh_convenience_kestrel
units.text: Update: the one-egg man bought two eggs tonight. I said 'big night?' He said 'my daughter's visiting'. I gave him a third egg for free. He looked at it for a long time. Then he said 'thank you' very formally, like I'd handed him a medal. Best transaction of the year.

units.author: lh_student_kestrel
units.text: I'm not crying in the lab, you're crying in the lab. also update: facilities say they'll 'look at' the corridor sensor. it switched on four times tonight and nobody came. I've started waving at it. it doesn't wave back. it's a sensor. I've been awake for 31 hours.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: Rin, 31 hours is the point where your brain starts filling in what your eyes miss, and corridors with lights going on are perfect for it. Please go home and sleep for six hours. Then wave at the sensor. If it still switches on for nobody when you've slept, I'll take it seriously, I promise.

units.author: lh_crane_halvard
units.text: From 60 metres up: a paperback about mountaineers that I read between lifts, which feels right. Nothing else up here but the city lights and the radio. When the banksman calls a lift I put the book face down on the dash and the mountaineers wait for me. They're very patient. They've been on the same ledge for three nights.

units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: What a lovely image: a crane cab with a book face down on the dash and a whole expedition waiting. I'll put one by in the shop for you if you ever pass through Tollinby, something with a summit at the end. My sea novel's crew still haven't sighted land. I'm rationing it.
